from typing import Any, Hashable, Optional

class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        if isinstance(capacity, bool) or not isinstance(capacity, int) or capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be a positive integer")

        if key not in self.cache:

    def put(self, key: Hashable, value: Any) -> None:

from collections import OrderedDict
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        if not isinstance(capacity, int) or isinstance(capacity, bool) or capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be a positive integer")
        self._capacity = capacity
        self._cache = OrderedDict()
    def get(self, key):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
            return self._cache[key]
        return None
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache[key] = value
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
        else:
            self._cache[key] = value
            if len(self._cache) > self._capacity:
                self._cache.popitem(last=False)
    def __len__(self): return len(self._cache)
    def __contains__(self, key): return key in self._cache

class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        if not isinstance(capacity, int) or isinstance(capacity, bool) or capacity <= 0:

from collections import OrderedDict
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        if not isinstance(capacity, int) or isinstance(capacity, bool) or capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be a positive integer")
        self._capacity = capacity
        self._cache = OrderedDict()
    def get(self, key):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
            return self._cache[key]
        return None
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache[key] = value
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
        else:
            self._cache[key] = value
            if len(self._cache) > self._capacity:
                self._cache.popitem(last=False)
    def __len__(self): return len(self._cache)
    def __contains__(self, key): return key in self._cache

from collections import OrderedDict
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        if not isinstance(capacity, int) or isinstance(capacity, bool) or capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be a positive integer")
        self._capacity = capacity
        self._cache = OrderedDict()
    def get(self, key):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
            return self._cache[key]
        return None
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self._cache:
            self._cache[key] = value
            self._cache.move_to_end(key)
        else:
            self._cache[key] = value
            if len(self._cache) > self._capacity:
                self._cache.popitem(last=False)
    def __len__(self): return len(self._cache)
    def __contains__(self, key): return key in self._cache

Let's think deeply about speculative decoding. It's a technique to speed up autoregressive LLM inference. A smaller draft model (or n-gram / self-drafting) proposes k candidate tokens (or a sequence) in parallel/cheaply. Target model verifies these k tokens in one forward pass (due to causal attention, can compute logits for all positions at once). Then acceptance: For each proposed token, sample from target distribution adjusted to match target's marginal distribution. Standard algorithm: given draft p_d(x_t | x_<t) and target p_t(x_t | x_<t). For each token x_t proposed, accept with probability min(1, p_t(x_t)/p_d(x_t)). If rejected at position t, resample a token from adjusted distribution: p'(x) = max(p_t(x)-p_d(x), 0) normalized? More precisely for speculative sampling: For each proposed token x_t, compute alpha_t = p_t(x_t)/p_d(x_t). Accept if u ~ U(0,1) < alpha_t. If accept, append. If reject, sample y from distribution q_t(x) = max(p_t(x)-p_d(x),0)/Z_t, append y, and stop (discard rest of draft). This ensures output distribution exactly matches target model's distribution (if target sampling is used and draft arbitrary). For greedy decoding, acceptance if target argmax equals draft token; if not, use target argmax and stop. For temperature/top-p etc, need adjust to preserve target distribution; many implementations use target logits and draft probabilities. If draft is deterministic or p_d zero, handle zeros. If draft model is same target? self-speculative.

Verification: target model forward pass over prefix + draft tokens. It computes logits at each draft position. Because of causality, one pass gives all needed next-token distributions. Need check memory, KV cache. The target's logits at position i correspond to token i+1? Let's define: prefix length n, draft tokens d_1..d_k. Input sequence prefix + d_1..d_k. Target forward computes logits for positions n+1..n+k (after each draft token) to predict next token. For d_i, target distribution p_t_i over next token given prefix + d_1..d_{i-1}. Compare to draft distribution p_d_i. Accept/reject sequentially. If all accepted, gain k+1 tokens per target forward (because target also produced a token after k? In standard, if all k accepted, you get k+1 tokens: k draft accepted plus one extra target-sampled token from the final target logits at position n+k, often called bonus token. If reject at i, you get i accepted tokens + one resampled correction token = i+1 tokens, and discard remaining draft. Need mention.

Why speed depends on workload: acceptance rate (alpha) and draft length. Speedup roughly (k+1)/(1 + cost_draft/target_cost?) More nuanced. If draft cost negligible, speedup ~ expected accepted tokens per target pass. Expected accepted tokens = sum_{i=1}^k prod_{j=1}^i alpha_j + 1? For independent acceptance. If acceptance rate high, more tokens per verification. If low, you pay draft + verification overhead and may be slower. Workload affects token predictability: code, math, repetitive text, templates, constrained outputs have high acceptance; open-ended creative/low-temperature? Actually temperature affects acceptance? Draft and target both sampled? For greedy, acceptance depends on target's confidence and draft alignment. Workload domain, prompt length, context length, batch size, batch size, batch size, GPU memory, model size, draft model size, hardware, quantization, quantization, KV cache, attention implementation. Also target model cost per token vs draft cost. For large target and small draft, draft cheap. For small target, overhead may dominate. Batching: speculative decoding can interact with continuous batching; if batch has mixed acceptance rates, need synchronization? Some systems verify per sequence; overhead. Long context: verification cost grows with context length (attention O(n^2) or O(n) with flash), draft cost

Let's think deeply about speculative decoding. It's a technique to speed up autoregressive LLM inference. A smaller draft model (or n-gram / self-drafting) proposes k candidate tokens (or a sequence) in parallel/cheaply. Target model verifies these k tokens in one forward pass (due to causal attention, can compute logits for all positions at once). Then acceptance: For each proposed token, sample from target distribution adjusted to match target's marginal distribution. Standard algorithm: given draft p_d(x_t | x_<t) and target p_t(x_t | x_<t). For each token x_t proposed, accept with probability min(1, p_t(x_t)/p_d(x_t)). If rejected at position t, resample a token from adjusted distribution: p'(x) = max(p_t(x)-p_d(x), 0) normalized? More precisely for speculative sampling: For each proposed token x_t, compute alpha_t = p_t(x_t)/p_d(x_t). Accept if u ~ U(0,1) < alpha_t. If accept, append. If reject, sample y from distribution q_t(x) = max(p_t(x)-p_d(x),0)/Z_t, append y, and stop (discard rest of draft). This ensures output distribution exactly matches target model's distribution (if target sampling is used and draft arbitrary). For greedy decoding, acceptance if target argmax equals draft token; if not, use target argmax and stop. For temperature/top-p etc, need adjust to preserve target distribution; many implementations use target logits and draft probabilities. If draft is deterministic or p_d zero, handle zeros. If draft model is same target? self-speculative.

Verification: target model forward pass over prefix + draft tokens. It computes logits at each draft position. Because of causality, one pass gives all needed next-token distributions. Need check memory, KV cache. The target's logits at position i correspond to token i+1? Let's define: prefix length n, draft tokens d_1..d_k. Input sequence prefix + d_1..d_k. Target forward computes logits for positions n+1..n+k (after each draft token) to predict next token. For d_i, target distribution p_t_i over next token given prefix + d_1..d_{i-1}. Compare to draft distribution p_d_i. Accept/reject sequentially. If all accepted, gain k+1 tokens per target forward (because target also produced a token after k? In standard, if all k accepted, you get k+1 tokens: k draft accepted plus one extra target-sampled token from the final target logits at position n+k, often called bonus token. If reject at i, you get i accepted tokens + one resampled correction token = i+1 tokens, and discard remaining draft. Need mention.

Why speed depends on workload: acceptance rate (alpha) and draft length. Speedup roughly (k+1)/(1 + cost_draft/target_cost?) More nuanced. If draft cost negligible, speedup ~ expected accepted tokens per target pass. Expected accepted tokens = sum_{i=1}^k prod_{j=1}^i alpha_j + 1? For independent acceptance. If acceptance rate high, more tokens per verification. If low, you pay draft + verification overhead and may be slower. Workload affects token predictability: code, math, repetitive text, templates, constrained outputs have high acceptance; open-ended creative/low-temperature? Actually temperature affects acceptance? Draft and target both sampled? For greedy, acceptance depends on target's confidence and draft alignment. Workload domain, prompt length, context length, batch size, batch size, batch size, GPU memory, model size, draft model size, hardware, quantization, quantization, KV cache, attention implementation. Also target model cost per token vs draft cost. For large target and small draft, draft cheap. For small target, overhead may dominate. Batching: speculative decoding can interact with continuous batching; if batch has mixed acceptance rates, need synchronization? Some systems verify per sequence; overhead. Long context: verification cost grows with context length (attention O(n^2) or O(n) with flash), draft cost

For greedy, accept if argmax target equals draft token; else reject and sample target. For tree, verify many candidates, accept longest accepted path.
- Acceptance/rejection: acceptance rate alpha. If accept all gamma, get gamma+1 tokens per target pass. If reject early, less. Rejection triggers resampling and maybe continue from accepted prefix. Need mention distribution preservation.
